blocks.text: South Africa and Rwanda are set to be removed from a US trade initiative that has provided duty-free access to the US market for thousands of products from sub-Saharan African countries for 26 years. On Monday, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said US President Donald Trump intends to “terminate” the two countries from the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) trade preference program starting in January 2027. The program, which comes under regular review, was extended in February by Trump.
